body.statement: Every solution of \(A\Sigma+\Sigma A^{\top}=D(d)\) has the unique representation \[A(d,q;\Sigma)=\frac1\Delta\begin{pmatrix}du/2+qt&-dt/2-qs\\-(1-d)t/2+qu&(1-d)s/2-qt\end{pmatrix}.\] Conversely, every \((d,q)\in(0,1)\times\mathbb R\) in this representation solves the Lyapunov equation and has eigenvalues with strictly positive real parts, so \(-A\) is Hurwitz.
body.justification: The affine fiber turns a nonidentified matrix inverse problem into a two-coordinate exact feasibility problem.
body.gap: DettlingHomsAmendolaDrtonHansen2023 identifies the two-cycle rank defect but does not give this time-gauged unknown-diffusion parametrization as a polarity-analysis object.
body.consumer: The four sector programs and every explicit witness use this common coordinate system.
body.proof_tex:
Set \(B=A\Sigma-D/2\).  By the Lyapunov assumption,
\[
 B+B^{\top}=A\Sigma+\Sigma A^{\top}-D=0.
\]
Every real skew-symmetric \(2\times2\) matrix is uniquely \(-Q(q)\) for a unique \(q\in\mathbb R\).  Since \(\Sigma\) is invertible, this proves the unique representation
\[
 A=(D/2-Q(q))\Sigma^{-1}.
\]
Using \(\Sigma^{-1}=\Delta^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}u&-t\\-t&s\end{pmatrix}\) and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d,1-d)\), multiplication gives
\[
 A=\frac1\Delta
 \begin{pmatrix}
 du/2+qt&-dt/2-qs\\
 -(1-d)t/2+qu&(1-d)s/2-qt
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Conversely, multiplication by \(\Sigma\) gives \(A\Sigma=D/2-Q(q)\), whence \(A\Sigma+\Sigma A^{\top}=D\).

It remains to verify stability, rather than assume it.  Under strict diffusion, \(D\succ0\).  Put \(B_0=\Sigma^{-1/2}A\Sigma^{1/2}\), which is similar to \(A\).  The Lyapunov identity implies
\[
 B_0+B_0^{\top}=\Sigma^{-1/2}D\Sigma^{-1/2}\succ0.
\]
If \(B_0v=\mu v\) for a nonzero complex vector \(v\), then, using the conjugate transpose,
\[
 2\operatorname{Re}(\mu)\lVert v\rVert_2^2
 =v^*(B_0+B_0^{\top})v>0.
\]
Thus every eigenvalue of \(A\) has positive real part, and every eigenvalue of \(-A\) has negative real part.  Hence \(-A\) is Hurwitz.
